transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came because… well, it’s gotten embarrassing, honestly. I clean buildings for work, and lately just the thought that I might see a rat—like in a trash room or one of those old basements—makes me feel like I can’t do that part of the job. And I know, I know, most of the time it’s just an old building, people leave garbage out, things make noises… but it’s gotten so bad I’ll avoid certain areas or freeze up.

It sounds silly when I say it out loud, because my sister used to joke that I could clean anything, and I have cleaned some awful stuff over the years, but rats… I just can’t seem to handle even the idea of one being there.
When you think about rats, is the main problem an intense fear in that moment?

Yes… it is fear, definitely. Like, just thinking I might see a rat in one of the trash rooms or an old basement, I get so worked up I can’t make myself go do that part of the cleaning.

And I know those buildings are just old—pipes make noise, trash gets left out, all that. I’ve cleaned worse messes, honestly. But with rats, even when I know it’s probably not actually dangerous, my head just goes there and I can’t handle it.
Is your fear mainly only about rats?

Yes, mostly rats. I mean, it’s the thought of seeing one that’s messing me up so badly. Like if I’m supposed to clean a trash room or one of those old basement areas, I start thinking, “What if there’s a rat in there?” and then I just can’t make myself do it.

Which is strange because old buildings always have noises and smells and trash left out—my job has never exactly been glamorous, you know? I’ve dealt with all kinds of messes. But with rats, even if I know it’s probably not really dangerous, I just get stuck.
